what: The heuristic reconstructs the depot/customer graph once in new() by parsing visited and loc facts and by reading metric costs from grounded visit and return-to-depot operators. For each state it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, computes an MST connectivity estimate and a directed cheapest-insertion completion tour from the current location to the depot, and blends them. If exact capacity(), demand(customer), and load() variables are available, it additionally computes a capacity-aware nearest-neighbor completion with depot resets and a demand-weighted radial CVRP estimate. Missing folded capacity or demand variables simply disable the resource terms.
why: CVRP states are primarily distinguished by the current route endpoint and the subset of customers still unvisited. An MST is cheap and robust but weak, while cheapest insertion captures the clustered geometric structure visible across the representative instances and provides substantially better ordering guidance. Capacity constraints force extra depot trips, so optional capacity-aware and radial terms improve estimates when the translator preserves the relevant exact numeric variables. The design remains general, avoids hardcoded IDs or instance values, and keeps per-state work quadratic in the number of remaining customers.
